neighbours.label: a piece of a digestive-tract medical term (es|ophage|al, per|itone|um, diverticul|itis, colitis), as opposed to terms for other body systems
fire: Long-term reflux can damage the esophageal lining.
Surgeons opened the peritoneal cavity to reach the tumor.
She was admitted with acute diverticulitis and a fever.
Ulcerative colitis causes bleeding in the large intestine.
Tumors of the esophagus often block swallowing.
Fluid builds up in the peritoneum in advanced liver disease.
Barium is used to image the duodenal wall.
A hernia pushes the stomach up through the esophageal opening.
quiet: Long-term smoking can damage the bronchial lining.
Surgeons opened the cranial cavity to reach the tumor.
She was admitted with acute bronchitis and a fever.
Rheumatoid arthritis causes swelling in the small joints.
Tumors of the larynx often block breathing.
Fluid builds up in the pericardium in advanced heart disease.
Iodine is used to image the carotid wall.
A cataract clouds the lens behind the iris opening.

notes: Common words on the topic ('Coffee and cola can contribute to indigestion') were quiet in a probe, so the label is about technical term pieces rather than the topic.
